cards.explanation: The answer is False. Jacob sent his family and all his possessions across the stream (Genesis 32:23). Then the text says, “So Jacob was left all alone…” (Genesis 32:24). No servants, no helpers, friends. Just Jacob, the dark, and whoever shows up next.

The man strikes the socket of Jacob's hip. When the man saw he could not overpower Jacob, he struck the socket of Jacob's hip and dislocated it as they wrestled (Genesis 32:25). One touch, and the whole fight changes. I'd have tapped out right there, friends.

The new name is Israel. The man says, “Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel…” (Genesis 32:28). Later the Bible calls God's people "the Israelites," and the text here uses that word too (Genesis 32:32). I think Jacob walked in with one name and walked out with a brand new one.

The word is prevailed. The man says, “…because you have struggled with God and with men, and you have prevailed.” (Genesis 32:28). Jacob walks off limping and still gets called a winner. That's a strange kind of win, bakers, and I love it.

The word is blessed. The man doesn't give his name, but the text says, “Then he blessed Jacob there.” (Genesis 32:29). That's exactly what Jacob had asked for in verse 26. I think he got what he held on for, friends.

The reason Jacob gives is that he has seen God face to face and his life was spared. He says, “Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.” (Genesis 32:30). That's the reason he gives for the name Peniel. Whatever else happened that night, Jacob names the place for what he says he saw.

The answer is True. The text says the sun rose above him as he passed by Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip (Genesis 32:31). The man struck that hip during the wrestling (Genesis 32:25). The night left a mark you could see in his walk, friends.

The reason is that Jacob's hip was struck near that tendon. The text says, “…the Israelites do not eat the tendon attached to the socket of the hip, because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon.” (Genesis 32:32). The verse starts with “Therefore to this day…” so the practice was still going when this was written. One night at the river, and the Israelites were still keeping it all those years later. I can't keep a New Year's resolution past February, bakers, and this habit outlasted all of mine.
